free_tier.stated: No published total storage quota. Per-file cap is explicit: 'GitBook allows you to upload files up to 100MB per file.' GitBook's own docs ask-API, queried live, answered: 'I cannot find a documented storage quota or total storage limit per organization on the Free plan.'
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: Access token in the download URL is NOT enforced. A deliberately bogus `token=0000` returned the identical 838-byte file (same sha256), so file URLs are effectively public and permanent.

egress.terms: Free and CDN-served. Files land on `*-files.gitbook.io` (backed by `gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com`), fronted by Cloudflare with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000`, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

tooling: GitBook Platform API `POST /v1/orgs/{org}/storage` + a `?ask=` query interface on the docs. No rclone backend. Git sync (GitHub/GitLab) is a second, separate route.
chaining: Unlimited free GitBook accounts/orgs x 100 MB per file x unbounded file count (undocumented total). If the total really is unbounded this is per-record-unlimited; if it is soft-limited, the multiplier is free orgs.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: 100 MB per file. The only hard published number. Total org storage: undocumented (searched the docs ask-API, no figure). Retention: files persist while the org exists; no TTL clause.
